cards.title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
cards.title_cn: Adam Mosseri 表示，围绕人工智能的负面情绪“将会变得更糟”
cards.summary: 【The Verge】Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don't like AI, and it's…
fulltext: The Instagram boss said that worries about AI come down to ‘a fear of being left behind in some way.’﻿

Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don’t like AI, and it’s not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and long-form video for Instagram, Mosseri said he thinks there’s a trend of “more anxiety and more frustration and more anger about AI,” particularly in creative industries:

It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry.

Mosseri claimed Instagram doesn’t rank AI creators differently, but raised the question of ranking quality, saying, “There’s a lot of great AI content out there, there’s also a lot of AI slop. Do we rank AI content as well as we rank non-AI content? Probably not.” Talking about AI slop again after previously bringing it up in a New Year’s slideshow dump, he said he thinks the term AI “slop” is used “too liberally.”

Instagram began cracking down on AI-generated profiles in August, after launching a label for AI accounts earlier this year, but misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes remains an issue. Earlier this month, Mosseri said Instagram is “actively working out what to do” about AI fakes, but he noted, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”

Mosseri said Instagram is “now starting to require AI accounts to label themselves, because we think it’s important that people know if what they’re looking at is real or not real.” He also acknowledged there are fears around AI, including from creators:

I think people are concerned about a lot of things. I think they’re concerned about owning their content and models getting trained on their content. I think they’re concerned— there’s people who are concerned about safety. They’re concerned about job displacement, having AI displace whatever it is they do, if you’re a content creator or an engineer or a mathematician. I think there’s concerns about— I mean, fundamentally what I think it comes down to when you really have, like, a heart-to-heart with someone is a fear of being left behind in some way.

cards.summary_cn: 【The Verge】当被问及人工智能和大学生在毕业典礼上嘘科技首席执行官的趋势时，Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 在接受采访时承认，很多人真的不喜欢人工智能，而且……
fulltext_cn: 这位 Instagram 老板表示，对人工智能的担忧可以归结为“担心在某种程度上落后”。
当被问及人工智能和大学生在毕业典礼上嘘科技首席执行官的趋势时，Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 在接受采访时承认，很多人确实不喜欢人工智能，而且不仅仅是年轻人和创意人士。 Mosseri 在 Colin 和 Samir 播客中谈论 Instagram 宽屏和长视频的推出时表示，他认为存在一种“对人工智能更加焦虑、沮丧和愤怒”​​的趋势，特别是在创意行业：
情况不仅变得更糟，而且还会继续变得更糟。我认为，在接下来的几年里，我们将看到更多的沮丧和愤怒，有些是有根据的，有些是毫无根据的，这会让很多人感到困难，而不仅仅是行业内的人。
Mosseri 声称 Instagram 对人工智能创作者的排名并没有不同，但提出了排名质量的问题，他说：“那里有很多很棒的人工智能内容，但也有很多人工智能的废话。我们对人工智能内容的排名是否和对非人工智能内容的排名一样？可能不会。”继之前在新年幻灯片转储中提到人工智能“slop”之后，他再次谈到人工智能“slop”，他表示，他认为“人工智能”“slop”这个词的使用“过于随意”。
Instagram 在今年早些时候推出了人工智能账户标签后，于今年 8 月开始打击人工智能生成的个人资料，但名人深度假货等误导性人工智能内容仍然是一个问题。本月早些时候，Mosseri 表示 Instagram 正在“积极研究如何应对”人工智能造假问题，但他指出，“我认为我们尝试禁止该平台上的人工智能内容并不实际。”
Mosseri 表示，Instagram“现在开始要求人工智能账户给自己贴上标签，因为我们认为人们知道他们所看到的内容是真实的还是不真实的，这一点很重要。”他还承认人们对人工智能存在恐惧，包括来自创造者的恐惧：
我认为人们关心很多事情。我认为他们担心拥有自己的内容和模型接受其内容的培训。我认为他们很担心——有人担心安全。他们担心工作被取代，无论你是内容创作者、工程师还是数学家，人工智能都会取代他们所做的一切。我认为人们担心——我的意思是，从根本上来说，我认为当你真正与某人进行心与心的交流时，就会担心在某种程度上被抛在后面。

cards.title: Galaxy Watch Ultra deal knocks $184 off Samsung’s rugged LTE watch
cards.title_cn: Galaxy Watch Ultra 促销，三星坚固耐用的 LTE 手表减价 184 美元
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra has dropped to $465.55 on Amazon, down from its $649.99 RRP. That’s a $184 saving, or 28% off the recommended retail price, and it’s a strong chance to grab Samsung’s ru…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra has dropped to $465.55 on Amazon, down from its $649.99 RRP. That’s a $184 saving, or 28% off the recommended retail price, and it’s a strong chance to grab Samsung’s rugged premium smartwatch for a lot less.

This is the 47mm LTE model in Titanium Blue, and it’s built for people who want more than basic smartwatch features. It has a titanium case, a sapphire crystal display, and a large, bright screen that’s designed to hold up better in rougher conditions than a typical smartwatch. Samsung also aims this model at outdoor and fitness use, with dual-frequency GPS, multisport tracking, running coaching, and route-focused tools for time outside.

On the health side, the Galaxy Watch Ultra includes advanced sleep coaching, heart-rate tracking, and Samsung’s Energy Score, which is meant to give you a quick look at daily readiness and recovery. Battery life is typically around two to three days, depending on GPS use, connectivity, and which health features you keep enabled.

The 2025 Titanium Blue version appears to be a refreshed U.S. model, and this Amazon listing also includes an Amazon-exclusive 2-year warranty. It’s especially appealing for Samsung phone users who want LTE, durable hardware, and strong fitness tracking in one watch. It also carries a solid 4.6-star Amazon rating, which adds even more weight to this deal.
At 28% off, this is the kind of discount that makes a premium smartwatch much easier to justify.

fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Big-screen movie nights and split-screen gaming sessions call for a TV that can fill the room without blowing the budget. That’s why this deal on the Samsung 75-inch M80H is worth a look, especially now that it’s down to $697.99 on Amazon.

That price is $200 off the $897.99 recommended retail price, which is a 22% discount. It’s also the lowest price we’ve seen this year, beating the previous year-to-date low of $767.99. On top of that, this is easily its biggest price drop on Amazon since launch.

The Samsung M80H is a 75-inch 4K Smart TV in Samsung’s 2026 lineup, sitting as an entry-level step above the M70H. It runs Samsung’s Tizen smart platform and includes Samsung Vision AI features, along with common streaming and voice-assistant functions. For anyone who watches a lot of sports or plays on a current game console, the native 144Hz refresh rate is a big part of the appeal. Samsung also markets it with HDMI 2.1-class gaming features, plus Wi-Fi 6E support for modern home networks.

This model is also built around a Mini LED design, and picture performance is generally described as good for bright-room viewing. Motion handling and gaming response are also strong, making it a solid fit for fast-moving shows, live sports, and games.
At this price, the Samsung 75-inch M80H stands out as one of Samsung’s more affordable large-screen 2026 options. You can check out the deal here on Amazon.

cards.title: Chrome can now pull autofill suggestions straight from Gmail
cards.title_cn: Chrome 现在可以直接从 Gmail 提取自动填充建议
cards.summary: 【Android Authority】TL;DR Google is rolling out Gemini-powered enhanced autofill in Chrome, allowing it to suggest information pulled directly from Gmail. The feature can surface order numbers, package tracking details,…
fulltext: Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Google Chrome’s autofill is getting eager to help you out — a little too eager, if you ask us. Earlier this year, the tech giant started testing a feature that would let Gemini fill out forms in Chrome with information from across your Google account. Now, the company is bringing a more stable version of that functionality to a lot more users.

For reference, when we reported on the development earlier this year, the autofill update was limited to Chrome Canary. Fast-forward to today, and it’s rolling out to all Gemini Personal Intelligence users in the US.

Autofill has always been a reliable Chrome companion, but it has largely been limited to handling the basics, like your name, address, and credit card number. With Gemini and Personal Intelligence now in the mix, the feature can finally tap into your Gmail account to pull relevant information when you’re filling out online forms.

Note that in its initial Canary implementation, the feature could pull information from Gmail, Google Photos, and “other connected apps.” In its current stable implementation, enhanced autofill appears to be limited to Gmail.

According to Google, the enhanced experience will surface order numbers, package tracking details, and flight bookings directly from Gmail whenever you need them. So, next time you’re trying to check in online for an upcoming flight, you won’t have to dig through your inbox to find your booking code or ticket number, as shown in the short GIF above.
Similarly, if you’re trying to track down a FedEx package, the feature would be able to autofill relevant tracking numbers for you.

Whenever you tap on a text field and a suggestion is available, it will appear under a Suggested by Gemini section. Tapping the suggestion, as seen in the example above, highlights its source. This suggests that the feature could extend beyond Gmail. Lastly, this is also where you’ll be able to remove the suggestion in question or jump right into Chrome’s enhanced autofill settings to manage the feature.

Of course, this level of convenience comes with privacy concerns, especially considering how much sensitive information our inboxes tend to store. And those concerns aren’t even unfounded. Just last week, we reported on an updated Google policy that states the company can use data shared through Personal Intelligence to personalize ads displayed to you.

That doesn’t necessarily mean the enhanced autofill feature will leverage your Gmail data for targeted ads, but it sure does raise questions. The company, for its part, said all your sensitive Gmail data accessed by autofill remains encrypted. Plus, you get to decide whether to enable the feature and what it “can access via your Chrome settings.”
Google didn’t offer a look at how these privacy controls work, and since the feature hasn’t landed for us just yet, we haven’t been able to explore them either.

We’ll have to wait until the feature becomes available to get a clearer picture of exactly how much control users have over the feature. Enhanced autofill is now rolling out to Personal Intelligence users in the US on desktop, Android, and iOS.

谷歌浏览器的自动填充功能正变得越来越渴望帮助你——如果你问我们的话，那就有点太渴望了。今年早些时候，这家科技巨头开始测试一项功能，让 Gemini 使用 Google 帐户中的信息填写 Chrome 中的表单。现在，该公司正在为更多用户带来该功能的更稳定版本。
作为参考，当我们今年早些时候报道开发情况时，自动填充更新仅限于 Chrome Canary。快进到今天，它正在向美国所有 Gemini Personal Intelligence 用户推出。
自动填充一直是 Chrome 的可靠伴侣，但它在很大程度上仅限于处理基本信息，例如您的姓名、地址和信用卡号。随着 Gemini 和个人智能的结合，该功能最终可以在您填写在线表格时利用您的 Gmail 帐户来提取相关信息。
请注意，在最初的 Canary 实施中，该功能可以从 Gmail、Google Photos 和“其他连接的应用程序”中提取信息。在当前的稳定实现中，增强型自动填充似乎仅限于 Gmail。
据谷歌称，增强的体验将在您需要时直接从 Gmail 显示订单号、包裹跟踪详细信息和航班预订。因此，下次您尝试在线办理即将起飞的航班登机手续时，您无需翻遍收件箱来查找您的预订代码或机票号码，如上面的简短 GIF 所示。
同样，如果您试图追踪联邦快递包裹，该功能将能够为您自动填写相关的追踪号码。
每当您点击文本字段并且有可用建议时，它将显示在“Gemini 的建议”部分下。如上例所示，点击建议会突出显示其来源。这表明该功能可以扩展到 Gmail 之外。最后，您还可以在此处删除相关建议或直接跳转到 Chrome 的增强自动填充设置来管理该功能。
当然，这种便利程度伴随着隐私问题，特别是考虑到我们的收件箱往往存储多少敏感信息。这些担忧并非毫无根据。就在上周，我们报道了一项更新的谷歌政策，该政策规定该公司可以使用通过个人情报共享的数据来个性化向您展示的广告。
这并不一定意味着增强的自动填充功能将利用您的 Gmail 数据来投放有针对性的广告，但它确实会引起问题。该公司表示，通过自动填充访问的所有敏感 Gmail 数据均保持加密状态。另外，您还可以决定是否启用该功能以及它“可以通过您的 Chrome 设置访问哪些内容”。
谷歌没有提供这些隐私控制如何工作的信息，而且由于该功能还没有为我们提供，所以我们也无法探索它们。
我们必须等到该功能可用才能更清楚地了解用户对该功能的控制程度。增强型自动填充功能现已向美国桌面版、Android 版和 iOS 版 Personal Intelligence 用户推出。

Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.

That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.

The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.

Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.
As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.
The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

Google is making it easier for businesses to connect their apps to its AI experiences across Search and Gemini with the debut of its Connected Apps Platform.

Introduced in Gemini and Google Search earlier this year, connected apps let users securely link and interact with popular third-party services, then use them to take specific actions. For instance, you could connect to Canva to design a flyer, or to YouTube Music to build a playlist.

We’ve seen varying takes on the idea by other consumer-facing AI services like ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse. The premise is that such integrations could ultimately shift consumer behavior away from launching and using individual apps to instead using their favorite services through their preferred AI provider.
However, to successfully capture and retain consumers’ attention, there have to actually be a wide range of connected apps to explore.
Google’s idea is to open its doors to any business or developer that wants to reach users through Search or Gemini by allowing them to submit their own connected apps and monitor their performance.
The platform preview is currently available in beta to developers in the U.S., and will allow developers to build and submit apps that can be used across Google’s products.

To get started, developers would integrate with a cloud-hosted MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or Android MCP using the AppFunctions APIs, then use the Google Connected Console to register, test, and submit their app, Google explains.

Essentially, this process lets devs connect their app to Google’s services so it can be used with the search giant’s AI features. Developers can also choose whether they want their app to be available via Search, the Gemini app, or both.
After the app is live, developers can track traffic, latency, and error rates, and maintain control over their brand identity, such as their verified logos and authenticated accounts.

Similar to how SEO allowed companies and websites to show search engine rankings, this could well be one of the initial steps for businesses that want their services to be more visible to users on the agentic web.

Google already has over 50 Connected Apps available in Gemini, including from partners like Adobe, Experian, Localiza, Peloton, and others, in addition to its own expansive set of services, from Workplace and Photos to YouTube Music and Google Home.
These apps will now come to Google Search over the next few weeks. Search today has fewer integrations, featuring apps like Instacart, Canva, YouTube Music, Yahoo Fantasy Football, and others.
Google said meditation app Calm is another new partner on this effort, and that its app will soon launch on both Gemini and Search.
The new Connected Apps platform is in public preview for U.S. developers who sign up for the waitlist. Google did not share when it would become more broadly available.

今年早些时候在 Gemini 和 Google 搜索中推出的互联应用程序让用户可以安全地与流行的第三方服务链接和交互，然后使用它们来执行特定操作。例如，您可以连接到 Canva 来设计传单，或者连接到 YouTube Music 来构建播放列表。
我们看到其他面向消费者的人工智能服务（例如 ChatGPT 和 Meta 的 Muse）对这个想法有不同的看法。前提是，这种集成最终可能会将消费者的行为从启动和使用单独的应用程序转移到通过他们首选的人工智能提供商使用他们最喜欢的服务。
然而，为了成功吸引并留住消费者的注意力，实际上必须有广泛的互联应用程序可供探索。
谷歌的想法是向任何希望通过搜索或 Gemini 接触用户的企业或开发人员敞开大门，允许他们提交自己的连接应用程序并监控其性能。

谷歌解释说，首先，开发人员将使用 AppFunctions API 与云托管的 MCP（模型上下文协议）服务器或 Android MCP 集成，然后使用 Google Connected Console 注册、测试和提交他们的应用程序。
从本质上讲，这个过程让开发人员将他们的应用程序连接到谷歌的服务，以便它可以与搜索巨头的人工智能功能一起使用。开发人员还可以选择是否希望通过搜索、Gemini 应用程序或两者都提供他们的应用程序。
应用程序上线后，开发人员可以跟踪流量、延迟和错误率，并保持对其品牌标识的控制，例如经过验证的徽标和经过身份验证的帐户。

这些应用程序将在未来几周内出现在 Google 搜索中。如今的搜索集成较少，主要包括 Instacart、Canva、YouTube Music、Yahoo Fantasy Football 等应用程序。

The expanded autofill capabilities can retrieve details such as a shipment’s tracking number, travel details like a flight booking number or hotel reservation, or the order number of a recent purchase. Sensitive data presented as a suggestion while completing a form remains encrypted, and users can manage what enhanced autofill has access to in Chrome’s settings, or turn it off completely.

Google is starting to roll out the enhanced autofill improvements today in the US. They’ll be available through Gemini in Chrome for users with Personal Intelligence turned on in the desktop, Android, and iOS versions of the browser.
